deliverables: Allocate capital to builders expected to advance Cardano Vision 2030 KPIs.
Require funded projects to track monthly active users, TVL, and on-chain transactions.
Coordinate proposal evaluation, feedback, transparent fund distribution, and results tracking.
Operate milestone-based disbursement from an independent multisig after administrator validation.
Return unused or unallocated DAO treasury funds to the Cardano Treasury.
request.recipient: Cardano Builder DAO, with treasury withdrawal received and administered by an independent council composed of dRep DAO members before milestone-based disbursement.
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund the Cardano Builder DAO as a smart contract-governed, KPI-driven funding mechanism for Cardano builders.

claims.claim: The Cardano Builder DAO is proposed as an ecosystem-wide, smart contract-governed funding mechanism for projects advancing Cardano Vision 2030 KPIs.
The DAO intends to allocate capital to builders who can improve monthly active users, monthly on-chain transactions, and TVL.
The proposal states that funded projects are required to track monthly active users, TVL, and on-chain transactions.
The DAO says it built Version 1 and Version 2 of a KPI dashboard, moving from self-reported KPI tracking toward live on-chain Cardano data.
The CB DAO claims it has already distributed 11.1 million ADA across 34 proposals in two funding rounds.
Round 1 is described as involving 38 voting members, 27 requesting members, 20 funded companies, 83% governance participation, and 5,541,335 ADA distributed through a smart contract-governed process.
Round 2 is described as adding 18 new members, funding 14 companies, and reaching 88% member participation after review, debate, temperature checks, and final voting.

The proposal states that official Cardano developer documentation describes CB DAO as a smart contract-governed mechanism with more than 50 established Cardano projects participating in funding decisions.

The administrator council is expected to hold funds in auditable separate accounts, avoid stake-pool delegation, delegate voting to predefined abstain, and disburse milestones through an independent multisig.
The CB DAO states it returned 354,790 ADA of unused funds to the treasury after its first two governance rounds, citing an Adastat transaction link.

summary: The document requests 20,000,000 ADA for Cardano Builder DAO, presenting prior funding rounds, KPI-oriented governance, administrator controls, milestone disbursement, and repayment commitments, but the deterministic assessment reports missing budget, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
